title: A Wasp Walls Its Nest Shut With Up to 13 Dead Ants
subject: bone-house wasp

scenes.text: This wasp's front door is a pile of ant corpses.
The bone-house wasp, found in 2014 in a Chinese forest. She hunts spiders, paralyses them, and seals one into each cell for a larva to eat.
Then she builds one last chamber at the entrance and packs it with dead ants, as many as thirteen.
Not food. The larvae never touch them. The ants are a big, aggressive species that swarms anything near their trail.
Dead, they still smell like trouble. Nests with the ant wall were raided by parasites about three percent of the time. Other wasps nearby, sixteen.
Fake a dangerous neighbour and your enemies stay away. A door made of corpses, and it works.

description:
The bone-house wasp, discovered in southeast China in 2014, seals its nest with a chamber packed with up to 13 dead ants.
The spider-hunting wasp stocks each brood cell with a paralysed spider, then fills the outermost chamber with corpses of a large, aggressive ant species. The ants are not eaten; their scent appears to deter parasitic wasps. In the study, ant-walled nests were parasitised about 3 percent of the time versus about 16 percent for other cavity-nesting wasps.
What is the smartest nest defence you have seen in nature?

first_comment: The researchers found 73 of these nests in bamboo tubes they set out as traps. Which animal builds the strangest home?
